decided.cycle: The day of each month's maximum (25, 55, 84, 114, 144, 173, ... 704) moves forward by 29 to 30 days every month, for all 24 months. That points to a recurring peak about every 29.5 days.
decided.week: Only monthly medians and maxima are given, so a 7-day rhythm cannot be seen.
decided.level: Year-1 monthly medians average about 590; year-2 monthly medians average about 465. That is roughly 20% lower.
decided.year: Both years have their lowest medians in June-July and higher ones in autumn (September-October) and the early months. The match is only rough, and the year-2 spring is weaker.
decided.highest_day: The largest monthly maximum is 3959, on day 291.
decided.second_day: Day 262 (3803) is the largest maximum more than 14 days from day 291, as it is 29 days away.
decided.peak_shape: Only the single maximum day per month is given. Nothing shows the neighbouring days.
decided.drops: Minima are not given, only medians and maxima.
decided.stands_out: Every month has one spike 3 to 6 times its median, recurring regularly. So the spikes are a periodic pattern rather than singular events. Nothing beyond that can be resolved from this rendering.

answer.guess: Something tied to the lunar cycle (for example, interest or activity around each full moon).
